spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** Cloud object stores (S3, GCS, ADLS) lack atomic multi-file commits, and Hive-style directory listings (`s3://bucket/dt=2026-11-18/`) stall on millions of partitions.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts Catalog Pointer -> Snapshot -> Manifest List -> Parquet Data Files (Catalog (S3 Atomic CAS) -> Snapshot Manifest List -> Manifest Files (Avro) -> Parquet); Concurrent Writers -> Optimistic Catalog CAS -> Async Compaction (Flink / Spark Writers -> Catalog CAS Commit -> Trino / BI Readers -> Async Compact + Expire).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** All three solve ACID on object storage, with different strengths in multi-engine portability, Spark integration, and streaming upserts. Explore the end-to-end Medallion lakehouse system design and compare ETL/ELT, Kappa, and Lambda pipelines.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Explore the end-to-end Medallion lakehouse system design and compare ETL/ELT, Kappa, and Lambda pipelines.

learningJourney.title: What are Open Lakehouse Table Formats

explanation.foundation: Cloud object stores (S3, GCS, ADLS) lack atomic multi-file commits, and Hive-style directory listings (`s3://bucket/dt=2026-11-18/`) stall on millions of partitions. **Open table formats** (**Apache Iceberg**, **Delta Lake**, **Apache Hudi**) place a versioned **ACID metadata/transaction log** over immutable Parquet files.
explanation.core: Instead of listing S3 directories, readers consult the latest atomic snapshot pointer (`metadata.json` -> manifest list -> manifest files in Iceberg, or `_delta_log/*.json` in Delta) to get **snapshot isolation**, **time travel**, **GDPR `MERGE INTO` / `DELETE`**, and **schema evolution**.
explanation.deepDive: In production deployments of Lakehouse Table Formats (Iceberg, Delta, Hudi), watch how what are open lakehouse table formats interacts with tail latency, retry amplification, and partial failures. Open table formats (Delta Lake, Apache Iceberg, Apache Hudi) add an ACID transaction log and metadata layer on top of cloud object storage (S3/GCS/ADLS) and Parquet files, enabling time travel, schema evolution, concurrent writes, and Medallion (Bronze/Silver/Gold) pipelines.

learningJourney.title: Why Raw Parquet Directories Break Under Concurrent Writes & Deletes

explanation.foundation: Think of **Why Raw Parquet Directories Break Under Concurrent Writes & Deletes** as the intuition layer for Lakehouse Table Formats (Iceberg, Delta, Hudi): The problem: see what breaks without Why Raw Parquet Directories Break Under Concurrent Writes & Deletes under real concurrency or scale.
explanation.core: Overwriting a raw Hive Parquet partition (`INSERT OVERWRITE`) exposes partial files to concurrent readers or corrupts the table on job failure. Furthermore, streaming micro-batches every 10 seconds create millions of 50 KB **small files** that degrade Spark/Trino scans by 20x unless compacted with `OPTIMIZE` / `rewrite_data_files`.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, why raw parquet directories break under concurrent writes & deletes becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Open table formats (Delta Lake, Apache Iceberg, Apache Hudi) add an ACID transaction log and metadata layer on top of cloud object storage (S3/GCS/ADLS) and Parquet files, enabling time travel, schema evolution, concurrent writes, and Medallion (Bronze/Silver/Gold) pipelines.

ideas.title: Safe Snapshot Vacuuming
ideas.description: Never vacuum/expire snapshots too aggressively (e.g., `< 24–72 hours`) while long-running batch or ML training queries still reference older snapshots.

ideas.title: Hidden Partitioning
ideas.description: Iceberg derives `days(event_ts)` automatically from the timestamp column—preventing users from accidentally forgetting the partition filter and scanning the whole table.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement Lakehouse Table Formats (Iceberg, Delta, Hudi) without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: To keep storage layouts predictable as data grows, delta, Hudi), never write raw Hive-style Parquet directories for mutable production tables—use Iceberg, Delta, or Hudi for atomic commits, snapshot isolation, and partition evolution.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

learningJourney.title: Where Lakehouse Formats Excel (and Where OLTP RDBMS Wins)

explanation.foundation: Think of **Where Lakehouse Formats Excel (and Where OLTP RDBMS Wins)** as the intuition layer for Lakehouse Table Formats (Iceberg, Delta, Hudi): Scope boundary: identify where this pattern fits best and where simpler or async alternatives win.
explanation.core: Use Iceberg/Delta/Hudi for analytical Bronze/Silver/Gold tables; use Postgres/DynamoDB for sub-10 ms OLTP.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, where lakehouse formats excel (and where oltp rdbms wins) becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Open table formats (Delta Lake, Apache Iceberg, Apache Hudi) add an ACID transaction log and metadata layer on top of cloud object storage (S3/GCS/ADLS) and Parquet files, enabling time travel, schema evolution, concurrent writes, and Medallion (Bronze/Silver/Gold) pipelines.

benefits: Multi-engine ACID reads/writes (Spark, Trino, Flink, Snowflake) with GDPR `MERGE INTO` and time travel.
costs: Requires scheduled `OPTIMIZE` compaction and `expire_snapshots` maintenance jobs.

comparison.choice: Good Candidate: High-Frequency CDC Upserts (Hudi MoR / Delta DV)
benefits: Merge-on-Read (MoR) and Deletion Vectors absorb streaming upserts without rewriting 512 MB Parquet files.
costs: Read queries must merge base + delta logs until async compaction finishes.

comparison.choice: Avoid: Sub-10 ms OLTP Point Lookups
benefits: PostgreSQL or DynamoDB serves single-row ACID transactions in `<5 ms`.
costs: Object-storage commits take ~100–500 ms and are built for columnar scans, not row OLTP.

learningJourney.markdownContent:
```python
# PySpark: Iceberg atomic MERGE INTO upsert + Time Travel + Compaction
spark.sql("""
  MERGE INTO catalog.silver.orders t
  USING staged_orders s
  ON t.order_id = s.order_id
  WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET *
  WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT *
""")

# Time-travel query to a prior consistent snapshot
df_yesterday = spark.read.option("as-of-timestamp", "2026-11-15T00:00:00Z").table("catalog.silver.orders")

# Compact small streaming files into optimal 256 MB blocks
spark.sql("CALL catalog.system.rewrite_data_files(table => 'silver.orders', options => map('target-file-size-bytes', '268435456'))")
```

knowledgeCheck.question: In Apache Hudi or Delta/Iceberg Merge-on-Read (MoR) tables, what trade-off does MoR make compared to Copy-on-Write (CoW)?

options.text: MoR achieves fast low-latency streaming upserts by appending small delta logs/deletion vectors, at the cost of slower reads until background compaction merges them with base Parquet files
options.feedback: Correct: CoW optimizes read speed by rewriting full Parquet files on write, whereas MoR optimizes write latency.
Both CoW and MoR provide full ACID snapshot isolation.

options.text: MoR eliminates the need for a metadata transaction log
options.feedback: Both rely on the format's transaction log to track base and delta files.

learningJourney.explanation: Run atomic `MERGE INTO` for CDC upserts/GDPR deletes, query historical snapshots with `as-of-timestamp`, and schedule `rewrite_data_files` to merge small streaming files into 128–512 MB Parquet blocks.

learningJourney.title: Comparing Apache Iceberg vs. Delta Lake vs. Apache Hudi
learningJourney.purpose: The trade-off: compare competing approaches across latency, consistency, and operational cost.
learningJourney.explanation: All three solve ACID on object storage, with different strengths in multi-engine portability, Spark integration, and streaming upserts.

learningJourney.title: Production Medallion: Streaming MoR / Micro-Batch + Async Compaction
learningJourney.purpose: Production architecture: see how the components compose end to end under real load.
learningJourney.explanation: In production, Flink or Spark Structured Streaming commits Bronze/Silver micro-batches every 1–5 minutes, while an asynchronous maintenance job compacts small files into 256 MB Parquet blocks and expires snapshots older than 7 days.

sectionDiagram.title: Concurrent Writers -> Optimistic Catalog CAS -> Async Compaction

cards.label: Optimistic Concurrency
cards.detail: Two writers touching disjoint partitions both commit via catalog CAS retry.

cards.label: Copy-on-Write vs MoR
cards.detail: CoW optimizes pure read speed; MoR + Deletion Vectors absorb frequent CDC updates.

cards.label: Safe Vacuum
cards.detail: Retain >=24–72h of snapshots so long-running Trino/Spark jobs never hit FileNotFoundException.

sectionDiagram.summary: Optimistic catalog commits decouple streaming writers from readers while background compaction keeps scan performance fast.

learningJourney.title: Medallion Lakehouses, ETL/ELT & Streaming Architectures
learningJourney.purpose: Applied problems: connect these internals to concrete system design and debugging scenarios.
learningJourney.explanation: Explore the end-to-end Medallion lakehouse system design and compare ETL/ELT, Kappa, and Lambda pipelines.

advanced.finalSummary: Never write raw Hive-style Parquet directories for mutable production tables—use Iceberg, Delta, or Hudi for atomic commits, snapshot isolation, and partition evolution.
advanced.summary: Open table formats (Delta Lake, Apache Iceberg, Apache Hudi) add an ACID transaction log and metadata layer on top of cloud object storage (S3/GCS/ADLS) and Parquet files, enabling time travel, schema evolution, concurrent writes, and Medallion (Bronze/Silver/Gold) pipelines.
advanced.keyTakeaway: To keep storage layouts predictable as data grows, Delta, Hudi), never write raw Hive-style Parquet directories for mutable production tables—use Iceberg, Delta, or Hudi for atomic commits, snapshot isolation, and partition evolution.

_recommendedProblem.title: Design a Real-Time Lakehouse & Medallion Pipeline
_recommendedProblem.prompt: Design a multi-terabyte Data Engineering platform that ingests clickstream and order CDC events from Kafka at 100,000 events/sec, deduplicates and enriches them in near real-time (< 2 min freshness), and serves BI + ML feature consumers via a Medallion Lakehouse.
